standard.title: Apply strategies to interpret and translate
standard.description: apply strategies to interpret and translate language in non-verbal, spoken and written cultural contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have developed strategies to interpret culturally-loaded language and can use bilingual dictionaries for translation (AC9LCH4C04). They understand register, untranslatable expressions, and cultural symbols. They have not yet applied translation strategies to extended texts, evaluated translation tools critically, or produced bilingual resources for community purposes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply strategies to interpret and translate language in non-verbal, spoken and written cultural contexts — including managing idiom and colloquial language, evaluating translation tools, and producing bilingual resources for real purposes.

nodes.label: Managing idiom, colloquial language and literal translation risk
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the risks of literal translation for idiomatic and culturally-embedded language, and apply strategies to interpret such expressions accurately.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two examples where literal translation would be misleading and explain the correct interpretation strategy for each.
nodes.typical_width: Examine the risks of literal translation in expressions, idioms and proverbs; recognise colloquial and slang expressions used by young people in the target language; develop strategies for handling language that resists direct translation; identify context-specific language across different social settings.
wider: Translate a text containing idioms and proverbs, documenting each translation decision — explain why a direct translation was or was not possible and what strategy was used instead

Compare a colloquial or slang expression used by young people in the target language community with an Australian English equivalent — identify what the comparison reveals about shared or different youth culture
nodes.hinge_reason: Managing the literal translation risk is the prerequisite for all translation and mediation work at this level. Students who default to word-for-word translation will consistently produce culturally inappropriate or misleading interpretations — undermining all subsequent translation tasks.

response_modes.reason: Translation decision-making requires students to analyse the source text, identify where literal translation fails, and select an appropriate strategy. Explicit translation task analysis — with documentation of decisions and reasons — builds this systematic approach before students can translate independently.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two examples where literal translation would be misleading
Explains the correct interpretation for each and the strategy used to reach it

nodes.label: Evaluating translation tools and resources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use and evaluate a range of print and digital translation tools, understanding their strengths and limitations for different translation tasks.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare the output of at least two translation approaches (e.g. digital tool and human translation, or two different digital tools) for the same text and identify at least two differences.
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of translation resources — print and digital bilingual dictionaries, digital translation tools — and evaluate their accuracy and limitations; discuss the differences between machine and human translation; create bilingual resources for classroom or community use.
wider: Conduct a systematic comparison of digital translation tool output with a human translation — document specific errors or inadequacies, categorise them (idiom, register, cultural reference), and discuss why the tool failed
Create a guide for using digital translation tools appropriately — including when to use them, when not to, and how to evaluate the output

response_modes.reason: Translation tool evaluation is context-dependent — tools that work adequately for some text types fail for others. Evaluating tools across different text types and translation tasks builds nuanced understanding of when and how to use them appropriately.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Critical evaluation of translation tools is a transferable digital and linguistic literacy skill. Background learners who can use and critically assess these tools — rather than being dependent on them — gain independence and accuracy that have practical value well beyond the classroom.
success_criteria: Compares at least two translation approaches for the same text and identifies at least two differences
Can explain when a digital translation tool is or is not appropriate for a given task

nodes.label: Producing bilingual resources for real purposes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce bilingual resources — community posters, event information, cultural guides — that accurately convey meaning across target language and English for a specific purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one bilingual resource for a real or realistic purpose, demonstrating accurate meaning transfer and appropriate language in both languages.
nodes.typical_width: Create and use bilingual resources for school and community purposes — event posters, cultural explanation guides, school signage, community information; compose resources that accurately convey culturally specific meanings; use both languages appropriately for the audience and purpose.
wider: Create a bilingual resource for a real community or school event — evaluate it with a target audience member and revise based on feedback

Reflect on the translation decisions made in a bilingual resource — identify which were straightforward, which were challenging, and what the process revealed about the relationship between the two languages

response_modes.reason: Bilingual resource production integrates translation strategy (node 1) and tool evaluation (node 2) into a genuine communicative act. The teaching investment is in creating real or realistic audience conditions — actual events, real community contexts — that give the translation task genuine communicative purpose.

success_criteria: Creates a bilingual resource with accurate meaning transfer in both languages
Demonstrates appropriate language choices for the specified purpose and audience in both languages
